chapter: Philadelphia, Atlantic City and the war years
title: Cuban Bennett gives Billy Douglas his horn
summary: Cuban Bennett, Benny Carter's cousin, gave Douglas his old trumpet before working for Campbell Soup in Camden.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Cuban Bennett. Kewpie.
Well, I mean he wasn't as old as
No. No.
Well, I mean how old a man would he have been?
Cuba?
No, Billy.
Billy, I guess, was -- Billy died. Billy was around -- at that time Billy was around about 30.
No more than that?
No, Billy wasn't younger. Billy was me younger than (unintelligible), because Cuba liked him

so much that Cuba gave him his old horn, and he kept (unintelligible) to play with, because Cuba went over to Camden, New Jersey, just across the river there, Delaware River, and went to work for Campbell Soup Company.
(Simultaneous remarks)
I mean that is where Billy Douglas got -- I never knew where that came from, Cuban Bennett. Well now, I mean, of course, Cuban influenced Benny Carter as a trumpet player too, I guess.
Yeah, Benny could play good trumpet too.
Yes, he can. But I wonder whether he plays like -- well, I don't know. There's something there because if Benny plays a very -- it's almost like a very good first trumpet, isn't it?
Yeah, that's right. That's true.
Huh. That's -- that's a strange thing, though, about Billy Douglas because I know Earl said he was wonderful.

Yes, he was. And Cuban Bennett thought so much of him -- see, he was over there when Cuban came over from Camden because, just like they go across the Hudson River to Jersey, same thing, you know, and Cuban gave him the horn.
Well, where did he hang out, Cuban
Bennett?
Well, up there on 132nd with all those fellows, musicians.
Well, what did he do?
Play music.
Yeah, but I mean where did he -- how did he earn a living?
He came out of Pittsburgh.
Yeah, but he never seemed to work --
Worked with small groups around the little, off side clubs.
Well, how did he earn a living?
(Unintelligible). Playing trumpet.
Oh, he did. Well, I always seems peculiar because he's never, you know, he's never --
Never got to the front.
Never in any bands----.
(Simultaneous remarks)

He was a fellow that -- he didn't care for the limelight. Like we'd be playing a place after get through with our regular hours and John (unintelligible) with the job. He'd come down. We would hire him, and that's what he liked, when he could play all night long and jam.
So that's very unusual. Was he married?
Not that I know of. He might have
been married in Pittsburgh, but he came up in Pittsburgh, but he came to New York.
That's strange, you know, because evidently he was a big talent, wasn't he?
Yes, he was.
I know Roy has spoken of him often.
Yeah, very fine. Fine guy to get along with, too.
Was he anything like Benny Carter?
Similar, because he had that nice ways. He never did criticize nobody, just pick up his horn and play, like Benny would do.
